name: Juniper Stream
description: A cool, oxygen-rich stream connecting every part of the valley.
roleDescription: Carries clean water, nutrients, and life through the ecosystem.

name: Oregon White Oak
description: A keystone oak that can shelter hundreds of other species.
roleDescription: Creates shade, nesting space, food, and soil stability.

name: Wild Crabapple
description: Spring blossoms become fruit that feeds wildlife later in the year.
roleDescription: Connects pollinators to birds and mammals across seasons.

name: Native Wildflower Meadow
description: A diverse meadow of lupine, yarrow, and Oregon sunshine.
roleDescription: Provides nectar, pollen, seeds, and cover for small animals.

name: Native Bunchgrass
description: Deep-rooted native grass protects the soil and stores moisture.
roleDescription: Reduces erosion while providing nesting and forage habitat.

name: Yellow-faced Bumble Bee
description: A fuzzy native pollinator active through much of the growing season.
roleDescription: Transfers pollen among flowers, sustaining plant reproduction.

name: Oregon Swallowtail
description: Oregon's state insect depends on native host plants and clean habitat.
roleDescription: Its presence signals a connected, plant-rich landscape.

name: Blue Dasher
description: Aerial hunter whose young spend their lives underwater.
roleDescription: Links aquatic and terrestrial food webs while controlling insects.

name: Coastal Cutthroat Trout
description: A cold-water fish sensitive to pollution, heat, and low oxygen.
roleDescription: Healthy trout populations reveal cool, clean, connected water.

name: Pacific Tree Frog
description: A tiny amphibian whose permeable skin makes it sensitive to water quality.
roleDescription: Controls insects and feeds birds, fish, and mammals.

name: Western Bluebird
description: An insect-eating songbird that nests in open oak woodland.
roleDescription: Balances insects and carries plant seeds across the valley.

name: Brush Rabbit
description: A small browser that needs dense cover near open feeding areas.
roleDescription: Moves plant energy upward through the food web.

name: Black-tailed Deer
description: A familiar Oregon browser that travels between forest and meadow.
roleDescription: Shapes vegetation and transports seeds in fur and droppings.

name: Japanese Knotweed
description: A fast-spreading plant that crowds out native streamside species.
roleDescription: Forms dense stands that simplify habitat and weaken the native food web.
